Casanova-Acebes 2021 establishes the pro-tumorigenic niche role of alveolar TRMs in early NSCLC: spatial localization, transcriptional reprogramming, EMT induction, Treg licensing, CD169-DTR depletion phenotype, temporal restriction.

First explicit demonstration that TRMs (not BMMs/MDMs) selectively induce EMT in NSCLC tumor cells via reduced E-cadherin, TWIST1/ZEB1 induction, and invasive protrusions in 3D Matrigel co-culture; tTRM-CM sufficient for migration.
First explicit demonstration of TRM-selective Treg licensing (CD73/CTLA-4 enhancement) in cancer; CD169-DTR depletion validates lineage specificity; spatial Treg-TRM co-localization in tumor lesions.

Applies Map17(Pdzk1ip1)-creER and Cx3cr1-creER fate mapping in NSCLC to assign group I (PPARG/MARCO/SIGLEC1) to TRM lineage and group II (TREM2/SPP1/APOE) to MDM lineage; cross-species conservation between human and mouse.
Identifies TREM2/SPP1/APOE/GPNMB as the canonical 'group II' MDM TAM signature in NSCLC, matching the MoMac-VERSE TREM2_Mac cluster #3 framework.
TRM-Treg axis is a parallel immunosuppressive mechanism alongside TREM2/IL4I1 TAM programs; relevant to general TAM-immunosuppression framework.

Casanova-Acebes 2021 (NSCLC-specific in vivo TRM-MDM dichotomy with mechanistic CD169-DTR causal evidence) is complementary to Mulder 2021 MoMac-VERSE (pan-tissue/pan-cancer scRNA-seq atlas of MNP states); the NSCLC group I = TRM aligns with embryonic-leaning MoMac-VERSE clusters and group II = MDM/TREM2 aligns with TREM2_Mac cluster #3.

Casanova-Acebes 2021 (TRM-driven NSCLC niche, lineage-specific) is complementary to Calafell 2024 (NF-kB/TET2-driven hypoxic monocyte-derived macrophage reprogramming): both papers contribute to the macrophage state-vs-ontogeny framework that the user's thesis builds on; mMAC1 maps to MDM territory (group II) downstream of the TRM-MDM dichotomy this paper establishes.

Casanova-Acebes 2021 independently identifies TREM2/SPP1/APOE/GPNMB as the MDM (group II) signature in mouse and human NSCLC, with cross-species conservation, consistent with pan-cancer TREM2_Mac accumulation reported by Mulder 2021 MoMac-VERSE.

Lazarov & Geissmann 2023 Nature review consolidates the LDF table mapping each TRM subset (microglia, Kupffer, alveolar, red pulp, peritoneal, osteoclast) to a specific lineage-determining transcription factor (SALL1, ID3, PPARG, SPI-C, GATA6, NFATC1) and the niche cytokines that pair with each.

Review consolidates the CSF1/IL-34/CSF2 trophic axis with tissue-specific dependencies: microglia/Langerhans cells require IL-34, alveolar macs require CSF2, most other TRMs require CSF1; bi-allelic CSF1R LOF causes paediatric leukoencephalopathy with absent microglia.

Review section on phagocytosis and nutrient recycling consolidates the efferocytosis machinery (TIM4 + TAM-receptors with bridging ligands MFGE8/GAS6/protein S/C1Q) and the programmed anti-inflammatory cytokine output (TGFβ, IL-10, PGE2).
Review section on Microglia in neuron homeostasis covers complement-dependent synaptic pruning and BDNF-driven motor-learning synapse formation, with disease links to ALSP and Alzheimer's.

Review section on Kupffer cells consolidates the iron-recycling axis (senescent RBC phagocytosis, haem-oxygenase processing, ferroportin export, transferrin transfer) and BMDM-takeover under high iron-recycling demand.

Review section on adipose macrophages consolidates Cox 2021 Science: WAT-resident macrophages produce diet-regulated PDGF-CC controlling adipocyte lipid storage; loss redirects energy to brown adipose dissipation. Mechanism conserved Drosophila→mouse.
Review section on tissue remodelling consolidates TRM=restorative / BMDM=pro-fibrotic dichotomy across liver, heart, kidney, lung, with CCR2-KO milder fibrosis as operational evidence.
Review covers TREM2/DAP12 LOF causing Nasu-Hakola disease, GWAS-confirmed TREM2 polymorphisms increasing Alzheimer risk, and disease-risk enhancer-promoter maps for microglia (Nott 2019).
Review reframes lysosomal storage diseases (LSD) including Gaucher as macrophage nutrient-recycling failure, with foamy-macrophage pathology and CNS phenotypes from microglial dysfunction.
Review highlights SIRPα-CD47 as the principal macrophage 'don't-eat-me' axis, exploited by tumour cells; targeting it is a 'promising strategy for cancer treatment'.
Review section on bone osteoclasts covers EMP/HSC chimeric origin (Jacome-Galarza 2019), osteopetrosis genetics (TCIRG1, CLCN7, RANKL, TREM2, CSF1R), and osteoclast-osteoblast TGFβ/IGF1 coupling.
Review summarizes the five PRR families (TLRs, NLRs, RLRs, ALRs, CLRs) of macrophages with examples and outputs, and notes inflammatory-PRR responders are predominantly monocyte-derived.
Review canonically extends the TRM-vs-MoMac ontogeny model with the three-wave haematopoiesis story (primitive / EMP / HSC), niche-LDF specification, and the ancillary-cell framing.
Review situates TRMs and BMDMs within the broader MPS framework while sharpening the lineage distinction.

Both papers organise the macrophage landscape — Lazarov & Geissmann 2023 from a developmental / disease ontogeny angle, Mulder 2021 from a single-cell transcriptomic atlas (MoMac-VERSE) angle. They are complementary: Lazarov gives the lineage and physiology framework, Mulder gives the cluster-level cell-state vocabulary.

Lazarov & Geissmann 2023 frames Kupffer cells as anti-tumour and BMDM-derived TAMs as pro-tumour — implicitly placing TRMs on the protective side. Casanova-Acebes 2021 inverts this for early-stage NSCLC, where lung TRMs (alveolar) are pro-tumorigenic. The Lazarov review predates broad appreciation of organ-specific opposite-direction TRM roles in cancer.
